title: Case-sensitive match
prompt: Show the full_name of contacts whose tags start with exactly GOLD in capitals, using GLOB. Replace the ___.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3');

solutions: SELECT full_name FROM contacts WHERE tags GLOB 'GOLD*';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT full_name FROM contacts WHERE tags LIKE 'GOLD%';
SELECT full_name FROM contacts WHERE tags GLOB 'GOLD';
wrongSolutions.why: Without *, it needs the exact text

title: Digits only
prompt: Show the full_name of contacts whose phone is exactly 7 digits, with nothing else. Use REGEXP.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3'); UPDATE contacts SET phone = '12345678' WHERE id = 13;

solutions: SELECT full_name FROM contacts WHERE phone REGEXP '^[0-9]{7}$';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT full_name FROM contacts WHERE phone REGEXP '[0-9]{7}';
SELECT full_name FROM contacts WHERE phone LIKE '555%';

title: Starting letters
prompt: Show the name of employees whose name starts with a letter from A to C, in capitals, using GLOB.
hints: [A-C]* is a range followed by anything.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET name = 'Abe' WHERE id = 12; UPDATE employees SET name = 'cara' WHERE id = 13;

solutions: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE name GLOB '[A-C]*';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE name GLOB '[A-C]';
wrongSolutions.why: Needs just one letter in the name

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE name GLOB '[a-c]*';

title: Valid club email
prompt: Show the id of contacts whose email ends with exactly @club.test in lowercase. Use REGEXP.
hints: Write the dot as \\. and anchor the end with $.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3');

solutions: SELECT id FROM contacts WHERE email REGEXP '@club\.test$';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id FROM contacts WHERE email REGEXP '@club.test$';
wrongSolutions.why: A plain dot matches any character

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id FROM contacts WHERE email LIKE '%@club.test';

title: Missing values
prompt: Show the id of contacts with no email or an email that isn't on @club.test.
hints: A pattern check skips NULLs, so test for them too.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3');

solutions: SELECT id FROM contacts WHERE email IS NULL OR NOT email REGEXP '@club\.test$';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id FROM contacts WHERE NOT email REGEXP '@club\.test$';
wrongSolutions.why: Comparing NULL gives NULL, so missing emails are dropped

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id FROM contacts WHERE email IS NULL;

title: Fix the anchors
prompt: This should find phones in the exact form 555-0000, but it also matches longer text. Show the full_name, and fix the pattern.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3'); UPDATE contacts SET phone = '555-01119' WHERE id = 11;

solutions: SELECT full_name FROM contacts WHERE phone REGEXP '^555-[0-9]{4}$';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT full_name FROM contacts WHERE phone REGEXP '555-[0-9]{4}';
SELECT full_name FROM contacts WHERE phone REGEXP '^555[0-9]{4}$';

title: Must start with a letter
prompt: Show the id of contacts whose email starts with a letter, using REGEXP. Upper or lower case is fine.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3'); UPDATE contacts SET email = 'Ken@club.test' WHERE id = 14;

solutions: SELECT id FROM contacts WHERE email REGEXP '^[a-zA-Z]';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id FROM contacts WHERE email REGEXP '[a-zA-Z]';
SELECT id FROM contacts WHERE email GLOB '[a-z]*';

title: Full email validation
prompt: A valid email starts with a letter, then has only letters, digits, underscores, dots, or dashes, then ends with exactly @club.test. Show the id of contacts with one.
hints: Combine a start check, a repeated character class, and an end check.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3');

solutions: SELECT id FROM contacts WHERE email REGEXP '^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*@club\.test$';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id FROM contacts WHERE email REGEXP '@club\.test$';
SELECT id FROM contacts WHERE email REGEXP '^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*@club.test$';
wrongSolutions.why: A plain dot matches any character
